extracted.intended_audience: researchers, peer reviewers, and journal editors affiliated with or interested in BMC Series journals and BMC's peer review practices
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of BMC Series' policies, practices and initiatives to open up peer review, support reviewers, and increase diversity and inclusivity across its journals. Includes guidance on transparent peer review, reviewer support/training, reviewer selection, and future plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness and accessibility (open access ethos)
rubrics_metrics.description: BMC's approach prioritises openness and accessibility so that the research we publish reaches an international audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review practices should reflect the publisher's open access ethos — making processes and outputs accessible to a global readership and considering how review policies enable that reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection based on experience and expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are contacted based on their experience and expertise and we approach researchers around the world to review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select reviewers for their subject-matter expertise and demonstrated experience. Proactively recruit internationally to broaden perspectives and reduce regional bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent peer review (publish reviewer reports; optional signing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The BMC Series has introduced transparent peer review: reviewer reports are published for all peer reviewed content and reviewers can choose to remain anonymous or sign their report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish full reviewer reports alongside articles. Allow reviewers the option to sign their reports or remain anonymous to avoid deterring participation (particularly for early career researchers or those concerned about revealing their identity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid requiring reviewer name disclosure by default
rubrics_metrics.description: The BMC Series pioneered open peer review revealing reviewer identity, but community feedback showed requiring names was a barrier; giving the option to sign a report allows reviewers to choose whether to reveal identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not force reviewer name disclosure. Provide flexibility to accommodate reviewers' career stage and safety/comfort concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and guidance for (novice) peer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide resources and guidance to increase clarity on the peer review process and increase reviewer confidence (e.g. 'how to peer review for beginners', BMC Medicine commissioned articles with tips for junior reviewers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer onboarding materials: how to respond to an invite, how to assess and prepare a report, expected timelines and post-review process. Provide targeted guidance for first-time reviewers and junior researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: BMC Series Reviewers' page: process guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: A central reviewers' page provides guidance on responding to invites, how to assess and prepare a report for a BMC Series manuscript and what to expect after reviewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain an up-to-date reviewer guidance page covering practical steps from acceptance of an invite to submission of the review and follow-up interactions with editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistics checklists and standards of reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors were involved in developing statistics checklists for editors and reviewers to use when evaluating the statistics in manuscripts; these are now part of our standards of reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standardised checklists to evaluate statistical methods and reporting. Encourage reviewers and editors to consult these checklists as part of the review to improve reproducibility and rigour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage and train early career researchers (ECRs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Initiatives (e.g. Nature Communications ECR program) specifically engage with ECRs to support them in becoming effective peer reviewers, provide outreach and instruction, and identify ECR candidates to expand reviewer pools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide structured training, mentorship and opportunities for ECRs to gain reviewing experience; identify and recruit ECRs to diversify and grow reviewer pools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative editorial model involving Editorial Board Members (EBMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: BMC Biology and BMC Medicine adopted a collaborative editorial model that directly involves EBMs in assessment, handling, and decision making of manuscripts, supported by in-house editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invite EBMs to take active roles in manuscript assessment and decisions; run open calls for EBMs and offer supported roles to broaden editorial participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer routes for researchers to apply to be reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals (e.g. BMC Biology) offer the opportunity for scientists to apply to become reviewers at the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide transparent application or nomination pathways for researchers to join reviewer pools, widening access beyond traditional invitation mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient and public involvement in peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Some collections (e.g. Patient and Public Involvement in Rheumatic and Musculoskeletal Research) allow patients, carers and members of the public to be involved in the peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include non-academic stakeholders where appropriate to bring diverse perspectives. Provide suitable support and guidance so lay reviewers can contribute meaningfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage alternative reviewer suggestions when declining
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewers decline an invitation, we encourage them to provide suggestions of alternative researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask declined reviewers to recommend alternatives, ideally including candidates from underrepresented communities, to help editors find qualified reviewers and improve diversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for diversity across demographic and career dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: We aim for gender, race, ethnic, geographic, career stage and other diversity in our reviewer pool; peer review invitations ask reviewers to consider alternative reviewers from underrepresented communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively measure and recruit for diversity across multiple axes (gender, race/ethnicity, geography, career stage). Include prompts in invitation workflows to surface underrepresented candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition and credit for those who contribute to reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Greater recognition needs to be given to early career researchers who peer review with their supervisor; we will look at how the names of those who contributed to a reviewer report can be included and credit given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create mechanisms to acknowledge all contributors to peer review reports (e.g. co-reviewer credit), and develop policies to record and reward such contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use reviewing opportunities to train reviewers on community standards (e.g. Data Notes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Build opportunities for early career researchers to review standardised format articles such as Data Notes so they can use their expertise to ensure community standards are adhered to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign standard-format or specialised article types as training opportunities for less-experienced reviewers to enforce community standards and gain reviewing experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evolve publishing practices with community feedback (open data & sharing)
rubrics_metrics.description: As research and community standards advance, publishing needs to also develop — e.g. the move to open data and data sharing; BMC will work with the research community and listen to feedback to make peer review more transparent and inclusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly consult community feedback and update peer review and publishing policies to align with evolving norms such as data sharing, transparency, and inclusivity.
